recommendation: Keep the source change. It completes the already-applied issue by removing a conflicting active source location without duplicating the full DiagnosticReport.encounter comment or changing conformance rules.
issue_request: FHIR-48767 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and asked that DiagnosticReport.encounter describe the encounter, when it exists, during which the reported data or specimens were obtained/acquired, while using ServiceRequest.encounter via DiagnosticReport.basedOn for order association. The final vote retained the word typically.
initial_application: PR HL7/fhir#3278, merged as 72e89a45b3b2fac6f33d372c6bb92da61dc80f48, applied the main DiagnosticReport.encounter comment change in commit e5e7f9730cf2cf4ca41940ae5911de6a16c38980. Current structuredefinition-DiagnosticReport.xml and the event mapping exception contain the approved comment.
additional_context: DiagnosticReport is active in source/fhir.ini and CompartmentDefinition artifacts are in publish.ini. OO WGM minutes and the associated Zulip thread show the work group wanted resource-specific guidance that recognizes encounter granularity, not an absolute rule or continued ambiguity about whether DiagnosticReport.encounter is an order/request encounter.
reconciliation: Changed source/compartments.xml so the encounter compartment note no longer uses DiagnosticReport as an example asking whether the encounter is when the report was initiated or reported. The note now preserves the general warning that encounter granularity varies and directs readers to each resource's encounter element definition.
source_changes: source/compartments.xml: Replaced the stale DiagnosticReport initiated-vs-reported ambiguity example in the encounter compartment note with general encounter-granularity guidance that points to resource encounter element definitions.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied technical correction on the same DiagnosticReport.encounter element changed requirements from request to report, reinforcing the separation from ServiceRequest order context.
